title: Self-Augmenting Retrieval for Diffusion Language Models
claim: Intermediate denoising states can query an external corpus mid-generation, so refreshed evidence conditions each subsequent step.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right timeline, query arrows up to corpus and retrieval arrows down
description: A single wide diagram with a gray cylinder labeled 'External Corpus' across the top. Along the bottom is a row of circles for diffusion states x^T, x^i, x^j and x^0, linked by black arrows labeled 'denoise', with a dotted arrow before x^0. Above each circle is a small colored box with a document icon (green, blue, red, orange), labeled 'Retrieved Context' in the left margin. The row of circles is labeled 'Diffusion state'. Upward arrows labeled 'query' run from x^T and x^i to the corpus. Downward arrows run from the corpus to the blue and red context boxes. The eye goes first to the corpus and then follows the loop of query and retrieval arrows along the denoising chain.
caption: Diffusion Language Models hold a noisy draft of the entire response at every denoising step. SARDI turns that draft into a retrieval query, retrieves new documents, and conditions the next step on the refreshed evidence. This way, evidence needed for later reasoning hops can be retrieved as the response takes shape.
abstract: Diffusion language models generate text by iteratively denoising an entire response in parallel, holding a noisy draft of the answer at every step. We show that these intermediate states surface salient entities early in the denoising trajectory, making them a useful lookahead signal for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). We further demonstrate that grounding generation in retrieved evidence sharply reduces inter-token dependence, making RAG particularly well suited to parallel decoding. We exploit both through Self-Augmenting Retrieval for Diffusion Language Models (SARDI), a dynamic RAG framework that uses speculative token predictions to guide retrieval during denoising. SARDI is training-free, retriever-agnostic, and applicable to any reasoning-capable discrete diffusion language model. Across five multi-hop QA benchmarks, SARDI outperforms training-free diffusion and autoregressive retrieval baselines at up to 4x higher throughput.
